ops.body:
**2026-08-29 — migration complete on both hosts. Every consumer released on daemonkit v0.23.0; both dead generations wiped.**

## Consumers — all 14, every one released carrying v0.23.0

| Consumer | Tag | daemonkit at tag |
|---|---|---|
| cc-skills (`plugins/codex`) | **v1.11.0** | v0.23.0 |
| cc-orchestrate | **v0.17.0** | v0.23.0 |
| cc-present | **v0.33.0** | v0.23.0 |
| reposync | **v0.29.0** | v0.23.0 |
| cookiesync | **v0.29.0** | v0.23.0 |
| binrun | **v0.3.1** | v0.23.0 |
| cc-patch | v0.16.0 | v0.23.0 |
| cc-notes | v0.51.2 | v0.23.0 |
| synckit | v0.38.0 | v0.23.0 |
| captain-hook | v12.22.4 | v0.23.0 |
| cc-review | v0.35.0 | v0.23.0 |
| fusekit | v1.19.0 | v0.23.0 |
| cc-pool | v0.68.0 | v0.23.0 |
| cc-interact | v0.32.1 | — |

**cc-interact needed no release, verified rather than assumed**: it constructs a `daemonkit.Daemon` only in `*_test.go` and `examples/echo/main.go`, has no LaunchAgent on either host, and its consumers resolve v0.23.0 through their own `go.mod` via MVS.

**binrun released as v0.3.1, not v0.4.0.** Its full transitive daemonkit closure from its two imports (`artifact`, `ghrelease`) is `artifact, bundle, durable, ghrelease, internal/flock, internal/realhome, version` — byte-identical across v0.21.0→v0.23.0 except a test file never compiled in. Notably `paths` is **not** in the closure: `artifact` resolves home through `internal/realhome`, never `paths.Agent`. So binrun's compiled behaviour is bit-for-bit unaffected and a minor bump would have claimed functionality that does not exist. Its release still exercised the fleet's **linux canary** — the v0.3.1 GitHub release carries darwin amd64/arm64 **and** linux amd64/arm64.

## Host end state

| Check | this workstation | forge-studio |
|---|---|---|
| `~/com.*` | **0** | **0** |
| `~/.daemonkit/agents/*` | **0** (directory removed) | **0** |
| `~/.daemonkit/a/*` | 8 daemons | 8 daemons |

**Negative check passed** — the plan's acceptance criterion, run rather than assumed. A decoy `daemon.records` was planted at the dead pre-v0.22.0 root `~/com.yasyf.cc-review/` and cc-review's daemon restarted. It came back healthy on `~/.daemonkit/a/`, rewrote its record there, and left the decoy **byte-for-byte untouched**. No fallback read survived either root move.

## The gate gap that caused this in the first place — closed

cc-skills missed *both* root moves because `scripts/fleet-build.sh` resolved a checkout by module **basename**, so it structurally could not build a repo whose module lives at `plugins/codex/`. Fixed in daemonkit `af2dbf5`; `ci/fleet-refs.txt`'s grammar is now `<repo>[:<module-dir>] <ref> [goos,...]`. **CI on that commit shows all 14 fleet-build legs green, including the new `fleet-build (cc-skills)` leg.** Two adversarial passes over the change first found five confirmed defects, three of them false greens in a release gate — see the note "fleet-build could not build a consumer whose module is not at its checkout root".

## Two hazards this migration surfaced, now recorded

- **synckitd and its helper consumers must move as one era.** reposync/cookiesync/cc-pool run as synckit helper *runtimes*, so the consumer serves the socket and synckitd dials it; different daemonkit majors compute different roots and they silently never meet. cc-pool's helper pairing was already dead this way before the migration started.
- **A consumer resolving its app path from `$HOME` splits from daemonkit's passwd-derived agent paths.** captain-hook's deployment landed in a throwaway home under Homebrew's sandbox while its agents targeted the real one — a failure that used to be loud and became silent when a 2026-08-07 Homebrew change made the temp home canonical.

## Known-broken, unrelated to this migration, tracked separately

- `com.yasyf.cc-pool.status.fusekit` fails on **both** hosts with `publish exact source fleet: catalog: tenant generation mismatch`. Proven independent of daemonkit state: it reproduces identically after a completely clean v0.23.0 state root. A separate session owns it. cc-pool's account daemon is deliberately left unregistered on this workstation — its plist still points at the stale 0.66.0 staged binary, and bootstrapping that would recreate the generation just wiped.
- `com.yasyf.cc-patch.watch` / `.heal` fail on both hosts on a drifted patch (`workflow-optin` matched 0 times against Claude 2.1.251).
- forge-studio's reposync/cookiesync `state.json` predate the envelope schema and are stranded — pre-existing (its synckit manifests directory has always been empty), tracked as its own task.

Closing this task.
